name: Required Growth Rate (Rule of 72)
description: Approximate the annual growth rate needed to double a value within a target number of years.
business_contexts: a board setting a growth target to double revenue within a set window
an investor setting a return target to double a portfolio within a set window
a startup setting a user-growth target to double its base within a set window
a lender setting a target doubling window on a balance
a planner setting a target doubling window for a population
question_patterns: Using the Rule of 72, what annual growth rate is needed to double a value within the target number of years below?
Given the target doubling period below, approximately what growth rate is required?
Using the Rule of 72, calculate the growth rate needed to double within the number of years shown.
What annual growth rate approximately doubles a value within the target period given below?
To double within the target years shown, approximately what growth rate is required?
solution_logic: Step 1: Calculate required growth rate = 72 / target_years
key_insight: The Rule of 72 runs in both directions — the same shortcut that estimates time-to-double from a rate also estimates the rate needed for a target doubling time.
common_mistakes: Reporting the result as a decimal fraction instead of a percentage (e.g. 0.09 instead of 9%)
Confusing this with the reverse question — this gives the rate required, not the time required
framework_soundbite: Flip the Rule of 72 around — 72 divided by the years you have gives the rate you need.
